summary: This informational RFC describes the namespace identifier mef for URNs naming resources published by the MEF Forum, which specifies and manages these resources.

plainLanguage.summary: The MEF Forum writes documents and needs permanent names for them. This sets up a naming system for those.

subtitle: Establishes a URN namespace for MEF Forum specifications.

tldr.problem: MEF Forum publishes standards for Carrier Ethernet but had no persistent, globally unique namespace for naming their resources.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7818 registers 'mef' as a URN Namespace Identifier (NID) with IANA, allowing MEF to assign persistent, unique names like 'urn:mef:yang:mef-services' to their specifications.
tldr.outcome: MEF can now use URNs to uniquely identify resources and manage them through the MEF Assigned Names and Numbers (MANN) registry.

today: RFC 7818 is an Internet Standard. The 'mef' URN namespace is registered with IANA and is used by MEF Forum to identify resources published in areas including Carrier Ethernet services, architecture, and operations.

sections.title: MEF Forum and Carrier Ethernet
sections.content:
The MEF Forum is a nonprofit standards organization focused on Carrier Ethernet (CE) networks and services. It publishes specifications in Services, Architecture, and Operations and Management. As MEF's work expanded, the forum needed a persistent, globally unique namespace to identify and manage resources like data models, interface definitions, and service specifications.

URNs (Uniform Resource Names) provide persistent, location-independent identifiers. RFC 2141 defines URN syntax. A URN consists of a scheme ('urn'), a Namespace Identifier (NID), and a Namespace-Specific String (NSS). RFC 7818 registers 'mef' as an NID, allowing MEF to create URNs like 'urn:mef:yang:mef-services'.
sections.plainLanguage: MEF is an organization that writes standards for network engineers. They need permanent names for their documents that will not break if the website moves.

sections.title: The URN Namespace Specification
sections.content: The 'mef' namespace is managed by MEF through the MEF Assigned Names and Numbers (MANN) registry. MEF controls uniqueness and persistence of the identifiers. The organization can permit secondary responsibility for certain defined resources if needed. The namespace supports experimental identifiers for testing, though these may collide if multiple users use the same values. The entire URN is case-insensitive. Assignment is handled through MEF procedures and documented in the MANN registry. Unlike some namespaces, the 'mef' URN does not have a Resolution Discovery System, so resolution is not defined.
sections.plainLanguage: MEF manages the list of names it creates. Each name is unique and permanent. MEF decides the format and what each name means.

sections.title: URN Examples
sections.content: The 'mef' namespace has been used to identify MEF's specifications for Carrier Ethernet services and architecture. URNs like 'urn:mef:yang:mef-services' identify YANG data models that define network configuration schemas. These names are stable and can be referenced in documentation and tools without risk of link rot or moved resources.
sections.plainLanguage: MEF uses URNs to name things like 'urn:mef:yang:mef-services' so the names never change or break.

references.text: Sollins, K. and L. Masinter, "Functional Requirements for Uniform Resource Names", RFC 1737, December 1994.
